definitions.explanation: To take air into the lungs and expel it, either as an involuntary bodily function or as a deliberate action.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}く{呼吸|こきゅう}してください。
{緊張|きんちょう}したときは{ゆっくり|ゆっくり}{呼吸|こきゅう}するといい。
examples.english: When you're nervous, it's good to breathe slowly.

examples.japanese: {患者|かんじゃ}は{自力|じりき}で{呼吸|こきゅう}することができなくなり、{人工|じんこう}{呼吸器|こきゅうき}が{必要|ひつよう}になった。
examples.english: The patient became unable to breathe on their own and needed a ventilator.

notes:
Covers both the involuntary act of breathing and conscious breathing exercises. The noun form {呼吸|こきゅう} is more common than the verb form and appears in many compounds.

Literally composed of {呼|こ} (to exhale) and {吸|きゅう} (to inhale), though the compound refers to the full breathing cycle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深|ふか}{呼吸|こきゅう}: deep breathing
- {呼吸|こきゅう}が{荒|あら}い: to be breathing heavily
- {呼吸|こきゅう}が{止|と}まる: to stop breathing
- {呼吸|こきゅう}を{整|ととの}える: to regulate one's breathing
- {人工|じんこう}{呼吸|こきゅう}: artificial respiration
- {腹式|ふくしき}{呼吸|こきゅう}: abdominal breathing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {息|いき}をする: to breathe — the everyday, colloquial way to say "breathe"
- {吸|す}う: to inhale; to breathe in — refers only to the inhalation phase
- {吐|は}く: to exhale; to breathe out — refers only to the exhalation phase
